p: "And you shall take for yourselves on the first day
the fruit of a beautiful tree" (Vayikra 23:40).
he raised a difficulty on what is stated
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפו, ב):
"And there is found in it 'the fruit of a beautiful tree,'
'Glory and splendor are before Him' (Tehillim 96:6), etc.;
and who is hadar? This is Tzaddik."
that it was revealed to him in a dream
that the esrog corresponds to the final heh.
And it appears from his answer
that the esrog corresponds to the Ateres Yesod,
and this is the final heh;
what is stated explicitly in the Tikkunim
and so it is in several places
וְתִקּוּן ו, כג, א — אִימָּא תַּתָּאָה;
the esrog is the heart in the middle;
וְכֵן כָּתַב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנו, א,
at the top of the amud —
וְעַל זֶה לֹא יוֹעִיל תֵּירוּצוֹ לִכְאוֹרָה.
and to this his answer would seemingly not help.
that what the holy Zohar says,
does not refer to the esrog;
and it is from the dew of Atika,
"My word shall flow like the dew"
which refers to Torah she'b'al peh,
which shines forth in the hearts of the chachamim,
and it is likened to dew,
whose descent from the heavens is not seen,
from the moisture of the ground.
And the flow from the dew of Atika
"Hashem my God, You are very great";
like the term 'great' regarding Hashem Yisbarach,
And of this there is no grasp at all
except through the garment of hod
"and they shall seek Torah from his mouth."
"for all that is in the heavens and the earth"
which we translate in the Targum
as "which holds onto the heavens and the earth" —
for it joins the Written Torah
Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמג, ב).
And the esrog is 'the fruit of the hadar tree,'
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעח, ב, וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת):
"The heh was a dalet at first,
and once it became pregnant with a yud within it," etc.;
of the Name Shakai, which is the bris
יְעֻיַּן שָׁם עַד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב;
see there until the end of the amud;
and it was explained at length elsewhere).
And the esrog alludes to the Shechinah,
and it is 'the fruit of the hadar tree,'
the lower yud, the lower Chochmah.
but it was not explained well.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 186b (Tetzaveh) — "When Israel are on the fifteenth day, He takes His children to spread His wings over them and to rejoice with them; therefore it is written, 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day' (Vayikra 23:40). 'Fruit' — this is the tree called a fruit tree, and in it is found 'the fruit of a beautiful (hadar) tree,' as you say, 'Glory and splendor (hadar) are before Him' (Tehillim 96:6). Why is it called hadar, and who is hadar? This is Tzaddik."

paragraphs.text: Recanati, Parshas Emor — The three hadassim allude to the three supernal Avos, "and these and these are the words of the living God"; and the esrog alludes to the Shechinah, and therefore it is held in the left, for from there she receives; and it is shaped like the heart.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction (2b) — "The three hadassim allude to the three Avos, the two willow branches to the two true prophets, the lulav to the Tzaddik — 'the righteous will flourish like a palm' (Tehillim 92:13); the esrog alludes to the Shechinah, and the sukkah alludes to Imma, who shelters over them."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

paragraphs.text: Raaya Mehemna, Zohar III 243b (Pinchas) — "The Shechinah is called the land (eretz) of the Holy One, as it is written, 'And the earth is My footstool' (Yeshayahu 66:1). From the side of Chesed she is called water, from the side of Gevurah fire, from the side of the middle pillar air; and she is the earth, the ground of them all."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 178b (Sifra DiTzniusa) — "The hei was a dalet at first; and once it was impregnated with the yud within it, it gave birth and brought forth the vav."
